propositions: A ticket directory with no CREATE or SNAPSHOT event causes the plan-relation reducer to fail, surfacing as an INDETERMINATE verdict on unrelated tickets whose relation graph walks through it.
Empty ticket directories persist in local clones and are invisible to git (git cannot track empty directories), so they cannot be spotted via git status or repaired by pulling shared history.
The plan-relation reducer must tolerate and skip event-less directories with a warning rather than failing the snapshot, because such directories carry no information needed for relation snapshots.

The writer continues creating ticket directories before their first event is written; reader-side tolerance is the correct fix rather than writer-side cleanup, which cannot cover process-death scenarios and races with concurrent writers.
